title: Live preview enemy HP bar ignores FadeOutDelay (UE fades on idle time)
body:
## Summary
The HUD theme live preview fades the enemy bar out at a hard-coded 6.0s, so the FadeOutDelay slider changes nothing in the preview, while UE fades after FadeOutDelay seconds without damage.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/HudThemeEditor/LivePreviewScene.tsx:23-29 computes enemyBarAlpha from literals 0.5 (first hit) and 6.0 (death) plus theme.fadeInDuration/fadeOutDuration only; theme.fadeOutDelay is never read in the scene. The UE widget (UE project Source/PoF/UI/EnemyHealthBarWidget.cpp:113-118, Visible state) enters FadingOut once TimeSinceLastDamage >= FadeOutDelay. The FadeTimeline (src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/HudThemeEditor/FadeTimeline.tsx:9-11) does draw the delay, so two views of one rule disagree. The literals also duplicate the scripted hit list in src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/HudThemeEditor/helpers.ts (enemy hits 0.5..5.0, death 6.0). Fixed = a pure enemyBarAlpha(t, theme) in helpers.ts that steps the UE fade FSM (Hidden/FadingIn/Visible/FadingOut, re-entry on damage) over the scripted enemy hits, used by the scene.

## Flow
- Enemy HP Bar tab -> drag FadeOutDelay 0.5 -> 10
- LivePreviewScene recomputes enemyBarAlpha without fadeOutDelay
- preview fade-out still starts at 6.0s, identical for every delay
- fix: derive enemy hit times from the hit table, step the UE fade FSM, read fadeOutDelay

## Expected impact
Designers tuning FadeOutDelay see its effect before applying to UE; measured as preview alpha samples differing between delays. Could break: the preview looks different at short delays (the bar fades between hits when delay < the 0.7s hit gap), which is what UE does.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the preview reflects FadeOutDelay the way UE does
Before: 0 of 80 sampled preview frames (0.1s grid, 8s loop) can differ between FadeOutDelay 0.5 and 10: grep -c fadeOutDelay LivePreviewScene.tsx = 0
After: predicted: frames after the last enemy hit (5.0s) differ by delay; fade-out starts at 5.5s for delay 0.5, at 8.0s (clipped at the wrap) for 3.0
Method: simulation - walked delay 0.5/3.0/10 against the UE FSM by hand; the FSM port is M and needs its own behaviour test
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: sample a new pure enemyBarAlpha(t, theme) on a 0.1s grid for fadeOutDelay 0.5 vs 3.0, assert the series differ after t=5.0 and match a hand-stepped UE FSM at 3 points; seed red by ignoring the delay

title: Shared StyledSlider does not wire its visible label to the range input
body:
## Summary
ui/StyledSlider renders its label in a sibling span with no association, so every range input it draws (11 in the HUD theme editor alone) has no accessible name.

## Description
src/components/ui/StyledSlider.tsx:39 prints {label} in a <span>, and the <input type=range> at src/components/ui/StyledSlider.tsx:47 has no aria-label, aria-labelledby or id. Per the registry technique accessibility/name-and-description-wiring the label must be wired, and per accessibility/primitive-level-a11y the fix belongs in the primitive (6 consumer files), not per caller. This round's accessible-name test (src/__tests__/components/ui-hud/hudThemeInventoryHardening.test.tsx) excludes type=range for exactly this reason.

## Flow
- open HUD Theme Editor -> any tab
- a screen reader on a slider says 'slider, 25' with no name
- fix: useId() in StyledSlider, id on the label span, aria-labelledby on the input, aria-valuetext = displayValue

## Expected impact
Every StyledSlider consumer gains named sliders at once; measured as unnamed range inputs. Could break: tests that query sliders by role+name start matching differently.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - range inputs are named
Before: 11 of 11 HUD theme sliders unnamed across the 3 tabs; StyledSlider has 6 consumer files
After: 0 unnamed, by the same accessibleName helper with range inputs included
Method: probe - the accessibleName sweep in this round's test file run over the 3 tabs; the fix sits outside this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/ui/StyledSlider.tsx:39 {label} src/components/ui/StyledSlider.tsx:47 6
instrument: drop the input:not([type=range]) exclusion in hudThemeInventoryHardening.test.tsx 'every HUD designer control has an accessible name' - red today, green after the primitive fix

title: Inventory stack-limit field snaps an emptied value to 1
body:
## Summary
Clearing the Stack Limit number field writes 1 immediately, so retyping a value after clearing yields 15 instead of 5.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/InventoryGridDesigner/GridSection.tsx:150 onChange = Math.max(1, Math.min(9999, Number(e.target.value) || 1)); an empty string is 0 -> 1, so the controlled input can never hold an empty draft. Fixed = a local string draft while editing, clamped on blur (the form draft pattern).

## Flow
- Grid tab -> select the Stack Limit text -> Backspace
- field shows 1 (written to hudDesignStore)
- type 5 -> field shows 15
- fix: local string state, clamp to [1, 9999] on blur

## Expected impact
Designers can type a stack size naturally; measured by a type-sequence test. Could break: the store lags the field until blur.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the typed stack size equals the intended value
Before: walked: clear then type '5' -> 15 (Number('') || 1 = 1, then '15')
After: predicted: clear then type '5' -> 5; blur on empty -> 1
Method: simulation - walked the onChange expression on the inputs '', '5', '0'
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: fireEvent.change(stackLimit, '') then '5' -> expect value '5' and store maxStackSize 5; blur on '' -> 1

title: Inventory Generate stays enabled with zero item types
body:
## Summary
INITIALIZE_BUILD_SEQUENCE is enabled when every slot type is toggled off, and the prompt then asks for an EItemType list with no values.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/InventoryGridDesigner/SummaryBar.tsx:30-32 disables the button only on isGenerating. src/lib/prompts/inventory.ts:85-94 builds slotTypeLines from the enabled set, so zero enabled types sends an empty list where the UE5 enum values go. Fixed = disabled with a stated reason ('enable at least one item type') when enabledSlots is empty.

## Flow
- Types tab -> toggle every type off
- summary shows TYPES: 0, Generate still enabled
- click -> CLI run with an empty item-type list
- fix: disabled plus reason text

## Expected impact
No wasted CLI run producing an uncompilable enum; measured by a render test. Could break: nothing known (zero types is never a valid inventory).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - an invalid config cannot be dispatched
Before: walked: 0 types -> Generate enabled, prompt slot list empty
After: predicted: 0 types -> disabled with reason; >= 1 -> enabled
Method: simulation - read the button's disabled expression and the prompt builder for the 0-type case
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: vitest: render InventoryGridDesigner, toggle all slot types off, expect Generate disabled with a reason text and onGenerate not called on click

title: HUD .h import report lists a repeated unknown name once per occurrence
body:
## Summary
parseUE5Config pushes an unknown UPROPERTY name every time it appears, so the report reads 'Unknown (not applied): Foo, Foo'.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/HudThemeEditor/helpers.ts:181 out.unknown.push(name) returns before the seen-set check, while a repeated known name gets one 'duplicate declaration' malformed entry (helpers.ts:182). The report (src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/HudThemeEditor/ExportPanel.tsx:25) joins the list verbatim. Fixed = dedupe unknown names.

## Flow
- Paste .h with 'float Foo = 1.0f;' twice
- report: Unknown (not applied): Foo, Foo

## Expected impact
A cleaner import report; measured by a parse test. Could break: nothing pins duplicates today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - each unknown name is reported once
Before: walked: 2 identical unknown lines -> unknown = ['Foo', 'Foo']
After: predicted: ['Foo']
Method: simulation - traced parseUE5Config for the 2-line input
Result: better
Gate: none

title: Two copies of the roving-tab keyboard handler in the HUD designers
body:
## Summary
ParameterEditor and DesignerHeader each carry an identical 14-line Arrow/Home/End roving-focus handler.

## Description
src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/HudThemeEditor/ParameterEditor.tsx:23-36 and src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/InventoryGridDesigner/DesignerHeader.tsx:27-40 are the same function body; a grep for a shared roving-tab helper (useRovingTab / rovingTab / handleRovingKeyDown) finds none in src. Fixed = one helper in a shared home (src/hooks or src/components/ui) used by both, with one keyboard test.

## Flow
- grep "ArrowRight', 'ArrowLeft', 'Home', 'End'" src -> 2 files
- extract the handler, import it in both tablists

## Expected impact
One keyboard rule for tab strips; measured as copy count 2 -> 1 with the tab tests green. Could break: focus order if the helper diverges.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation of the roving-tab rule
Before: 2 identical copies (14 lines each), 0 shared helpers
After: 1 helper, 2 call sites
Method: probe - grep count over src; the shared home is outside this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: grep count of the handler body (2 -> 1) plus an ArrowRight/End keyboard test on both tablists, red if either strip stops moving focus

title: 14 sub-12px text sites in the HUD theme and inventory designers
body:
## Summary
The two designers carry 14 text sizes under the repo's 12px legibility floor (ESLint warns on each).

## Description
npx eslint over src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/HudThemeEditor and src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/InventoryGridDesigner reports 14 'Text below the 12px legibility floor' warnings across the files (e.g. src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/HudThemeEditor/LivePreviewScene.tsx:96, src/components/modules/content/ui-hud/InventoryGridDesigner/GridSection.tsx:32). src/__tests__/a11y/legibility-floor-guard.test.ts:75 pins LivePreviewScene at text:1, so the ratchet moves with the fix. Fixed = text-xs or ui/MicroLabel per occurrence (TEXT_SCALE classification).

## Flow
- eslint the two folders -> 14 legibility warnings
- convert per occurrence, lower the guard's pinned count

## Expected impact
Readable labels in the designers; measured as the ESLint warning count. Could break: the 24px equipment stubs may need MicroLabel rather than text-xs to fit.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - designer text meets the 12px floor
Before: 14 legibility warnings
After: 0 warnings; guard pin lowered
Method: gate - ESLint warning count; not built this round because the 24px equipment stubs need a per-occurrence fit check
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: eslint -f json (HudThemeEditor + InventoryGridDesigner): {'Text below the 12px legibility floor': 14}
instrument: the ESLint warning count for the two folders (14 -> 0) plus legibility-floor-guard green with its pin lowered
